steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Line a baking sheet with wax paper; set aside.

Place chocolate and peanut butter chips in the top of a double boiler over simmering water. Stir frequently, scraping down the sides with a rubber spatula to avoid scorching, until melted, about 5 minutes.
Stir peanuts into the chocolate-peanut butter mixture until well coated.
Drop teaspoonfuls of mixture onto the prepared baking sheet. Refrigerate until firm, 30 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Clusters
raw_recipe.description: Peanut clusters are a delicious sweet and crunchy holiday treat that are easy to make with just 3 ingredients: peanuts, chocolate, and peanut butter chips.

review.reviewBody: I have been making this recipe for over 10 years now. The only thing I do different is melting the chips inthe microwave, stirring every 15 seconds till smooth. The spanish peanuts give them a wonderful salty taste...everyone asks me for the recipe. A Christmas tradition inour family!

I tried this recipe with lightly salted roasted peanuts and dark chocolate chips mixed with white chocolate chips. It was great! I tried it with almonds. Again it was great! I tried it with raisins using milk chocolate chips and then I tried it with pistachios using dark chocolate chips. Both were fantastic! This is a very easy recipe. I didn't leave the candy out to harden naturally the first time, I put it in the fridge and the chocolate was a bit hard. The next times that I made the candy, I let it set at room temperature and it came out perfect. There's no baking involved but it did take some time to harden. Here at my place it took 6-7 hours. It might vary from place to place depending on temperature I think.
I also used the microwave to melt the chips. I heated them on high for 30 seconds and then stirred really well then heated again, etc. I think it took about a minute and a half to two minutes. The chips do melt as you stir them.

I use red Spanish peanuts (which is what my original recipe calls for dated 1950) and butterscotch chips in place of the peanut butter chips. I also use parfin wax (from original recipe) with mine to help it stay firm. My family had been getting this recipe from me for years. I've placed it in cook books also. My family also request this every time I make them candy. Very easy and with so few ingredients you can't go wrong. I have also used This same recipe with raisins, cashews, small pretzels and pecans. 

I melt the wax first in a double boiler then add both chip packages and then the nuts. Dip by teaspoon onto wax paper on a cookie sheet. I either put them in the freezer for about 15 minutes or set them outside to freeze. I store them in Tupperware containers in the freezer till I'm ready to give them away.

These were so easy to make and so delicious! I also used Spanish peanuts based on the recommendations of others, and used the shortcut recommended by one reviewer to melt the chips in the microwave, stirring after 15 second increments. Both these edits worked out really well! I also sprinkled the tops of half with sea salt for some variety. Looking forward to bringing these to a holiday party tonight!

I did a double batch- two 12oz containers lightly salted peanuts, two 12oz containers semi-sweet chocolate chips, one 12oz bag peanut butter chips, and one 12oz bag butterscotch chips. I set up muffin liners on a baking sheet and filled them up about 1/3 each - this made just enough for Christmas gifts to those hard-to-shop-for people on my list. Very good, though very rich... everyone seemed to like them.

I made these for DH for Valentines Day, but I did use salted peanuts, instead of the Raw Spanish Peanuts. This is a favorite treat of his I usually only make for Christmas. I have always just used the Chocolate Almond Bark, which he claims he likes slightly better, as it had more of a Chocolate flavor. Will probably make this again, as I thought this was easier, as I just melted the chips in the microwave until melted, mixed in nuts, and put on waxed paper with a teaspoon. Start to finish was only a few minutes, which is a huge plus for me!! Thanks Donna!!

We don't care for too bitter or too sweet. So I revised the recipe just a little for our taste. I used 12 oz semi sweet chips and 8 oz milk chocolate chips and 4 oz white chocolate chips. Melted all in microwave. Added more peanuts than what it called for. Was great.
Sometimes I make these in the microwave, but either way they're perfect every time.
Yum. Here is what works for me: 1 bag of semi sweet chips, 4 squares of dark bakers chocolate, 13.5 oz can of roasted/salted Spanish peanuts. I like a high nut/chocolate ratio.
Delicious and super easy to make. I warmed the chocolate in my IP on slow cook, and used milk chocolate and semi sweet chocolate chips.
Easy and delicious. Have done stove top and microwave methods, stove yielded better results, but both were good. (Used roasted Spanish peanuts)

I used 1/2 dark chocolate chips and 1/2 semi-sweet chocolate chips. The flavor was not too sweet, but delicious and was a great hit. I will definitely be making this again. It would make a great, simple gift.

I used zero sugar peanut butter chips and dark chocolate. These got rave reviews from everyone who received them last Christmas and I am doing it again this year. Easy to make since I have a vintage double boiler that I knew would come in handy!
I make these every Christmas and give them away in pretty boxes as gifts.
Pretty good … I’m impatient to wait for them to cool off so they will set up though lol
have made these several times now and always delicious

I used creamy peanut butter instead of the chips. I think the chips would have been better. The peanut butter kept the chocolate from setting up all the way without going in the fridge. Otherwise, they were a hit :)

So easy and good! For one batch, I used 1 bag each of milk chocolate, semisweet, butterscotch chips along with 1 1/2 jars salted roasted peanuts. Had to use improvised double boiler to accommodate. Made 3 trays full. Takes a while to set up, will refrigerate before bagging up for gifts.
Added 1/2 peanut butter Chips and 1/2 butterscotch chips. Yummy!
I just made my second batch today. This time I used peanuts and cashews. Great, simple recipe.
